A.explanation: With $3X = 2 \times 720\text{ nm}$, $X = 480\text{ nm}$, which satisfies the same $d\sin\theta$ condition.

B.explanation: 540 nm would give $3 \times 540 = 1620\text{ nm}$, which is larger than $2 \times 720 = 1440\text{ nm}$ so the angles would not match.

C.explanation: 960 nm incorrectly scales the wavelength up with order, whereas higher order at the same angle requires a shorter wavelength.

D.explanation: 1100 nm is longer than the red light wavelength and would diffract through a larger angle for any given order.

hints: Notice the phrase same position on the screen means the same diffracted angle $\theta$ from the same grating with spacing $d$.
Recall the grating equation for normal incidence $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$, so $d\sin\theta$ is identical for the two cases.
Set the second-order red term $2 \times 720\text{ nm}$ equal to the third-order unknown term $3 \times X$ and solve for $X$.
walkthrough: The grating spacing $d$ is unchanged and same screen position means same angle $\theta$, so $d\sin\theta$ is the same for both beams.
Use $d\sin\theta = n\lambda$ for normal incidence, where $n$ is the order and $\lambda$ is the wavelength.
For radiation X: $d\sin\theta = 3 \times X$. Equate them to get $3X = 1440\text{ nm}$.
Solve: $X = 1440/3\text{ nm} = 480\text{ nm}$ with the same unit $\text{nm}$. This is option A.
